title: Finite henselian factor of a quasi-finite tensor base change
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a finite-type homomorphism of commutative rings, let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be a prime over $\mathfrak p\subset A$, and suppose $A\to B$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ be a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] with a local homomorphism $A_{\mathfrak p}\to R$, where local means that the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Put $C=R\otimes_A B$. For every prime $\mathfrak n\subset C$ whose contractions to $R$ and $B$ are $\mathfrak m_R$ and $\mathfrak q$, respectively, $R\to C$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak n$ and the canonical map $R\to C_{\mathfrak n}$ is finite and local. Here finite means that $C_{\mathfrak n}$ is finitely generated as an $R$-module. Moreover $C_{\mathfrak n}$ is henselian. No ind-etaleness, residue-field isomorphism or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $R$.

proof.text: Use the tensor algebra structure of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The square $A\to B$, $A\to R$, $B\to C$, $R\to C$ commutes. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and $r\otimes b=(r\otimes1)(1\otimes b)$. Thus the images of $B$ and $R$ generate $C$ in the precise sum-of-products sense of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-four-rings]. Apply that node with $(R,S,R',S')=(A,B,R,C)$ and primes $(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q,\mathfrak m_R,\mathfrak n)$. It gives both finite type of $R\to C$ and quasi-finiteness at $\mathfrak n$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-type-product-decomposition] to $R\to C$: write $C\cong A_1\times\cdots\times A_t\times D$, with each $A_i$ local and module-finite over $R$ and with no quasi-finite prime of $D$ above $\mathfrak m_R$. A prime of a finite product selects exactly one factor: among the orthogonal coordinate idempotents summing to $1$, exactly one is outside the prime (at least one because the sum is $1$, at most one because their products are zero); all other factors lie in the prime. If $\mathfrak n$ selected $D$, its corresponding prime $\mathfrak d$ would still contract to $\mathfrak m_R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-four-rings] with $(R,S,R',S')=(R,C,R,D)$ and $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak d$. Its contraction to $C$ is $\mathfrak n$, and $R\to C$ is finite type by Step 1. Surjectivity of $C\to D$ gives the sum-of-products condition (take the $R$-factor to be $1$). Thus Step 1 implies quasi-finiteness of $R\to D$ at $\mathfrak d$, contradicting the remainder clause. Hence $\mathfrak n$ selects some $A_i$ and a prime $P\subset A_i$ over $\mathfrak m_R$.

The domain $A_i/P$ is a finite-dimensional algebra over the field $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$: any finite $R$-module generating family of $A_i$ maps to a spanning family, since $\mathfrak m_R$ acts by zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field], $A_i/P$ is a field. Thus $P$ is maximal and, since $A_i$ is local, it is its unique maximal ideal. Let $\pi_i:C	o A_i$ be the coordinate projection through the product decomposition of Step 2. For $s
otin\mathfrak n$, $\pi_i(s)
otin P$ is a unit. The fraction formula $c/s\mapsto\pi_i(c)\pi_i(s)^{-1}$ therefore defines $C_{\mathfrak n}	o A_i$. Its inverse sends $a$ to the image in $C_{\mathfrak n}$ of the coordinate vector with entry $a$ at $i$ and zeros elsewhere. Indeed the coordinate idempotent $e_i
otin\mathfrak n$ becomes the unit $1$ after localization (an invertible idempotent equals $1$), and all other factors become zero. These formulas are inverse unital $R$-algebra homomorphisms. Consequently $C_{\mathfrak n}\cong A_i$ is module-finite over $R$.

By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $C_{\mathfrak n}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak nC_{\mathfrak n}$. The fraction criterion gives $c/1\in\mathfrak nC_{\mathfrak n}$ exactly when $c\in\mathfrak n$: if $sc\in\mathfrak n$ with $s\notin\mathfrak n$, primality forces $c\in\mathfrak n$. Its inverse image in $R$ is therefore $\mathfrak n\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$, proving locality of the canonical structural map. Finally apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-henselian] to this local module-finite $R$-algebra, with the given henselian ring $R$, to conclude that $C_{\mathfrak n}$ is henselian. All maps used are the canonical structural maps or $R$-algebra isomorphisms, so finiteness concerns precisely the map in the statement.

The diff against fc1b98b5 changes only Step 1 notation (R' instead of R\prime), the Step 2 wording (the second four-rings application is now written out explicitly) and the split_report summary. There are no repair notes and no new nodes. The statement keeps all hypotheses and is a correct generalization of the first two sentences of 05WP's proof to any henselian local R with a local map A_p->R, which is exactly what 04GH(3) needs. Step 1: the tensor pushout plus pure-tensor generation give the four-rings hypothesis for (A,B,R,C), so R->C is of finite type and quasi-finite at n. Step 2: the 04GJ decomposition applies and prime selection by idempotents is elementary. The remainder D is excluded by four-rings on (R,C,R,D): C->D is surjective, the inverse images of d are n and m_R, so R->D would be quasi-finite at d, a contradiction. Step 3: P∩R=m_R, so A_i/P is a finite-dimensional k-domain, hence a field (Mathlib leaf), and P is the maximal ideal of A_i. I checked both composites of the explicit C_n≅A_i comparison. Step 4: locality follows from the fraction criterion, and 04GH(2)'s hypotheses hold exactly, giving henselian. Edge cases checked: R a field (k[e]/e^2), C=0, t=0, a non-quasi-finite remainder, and the role of the m_R-contraction in maximality. A DAG grep for 04GH/05WP finds no duplicate: finite-over-henselian-local-product covers only the finite case, and the parent and 05WR siblings are different statements. I accept the declared tool uses: four-rings, the finite-type decomposition and finite-local-henselian, all generic algebra that the sibling node also uses. There is no SGA citation. No changes.
